summary: Source-anchored research for mongosh Reference. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Interactive mongosh output is not a stable substitute for JSON serialization: compatibility documentation describes unquoted keys and single-quoted strings. Use EJSON.stringify() for explicit Extended JSON output; the upstream CLI also documents --json=canonical or --json=relaxed for --eval results. (high confidence)
mongosh is the MongoDB shell implemented in a Node.js-based environment; its upstream repository contains components for the REPL, browser and Compass environments. (high confidence)

displayBatchSize controls the number of items shown per cursor iteration; cursor.batchSize() controls the documents returned per server batch. These settings address different layers. (low confidence)

The script guide recommends --file or -f explicitly because bare filenames can cause connection parsing failures when combined with other command-line arguments; load() has no search path. (low confidence)

Legacy mongo scripts need migration review: numeric values default to Int32 when representable and otherwise Double in mongosh, whereas the legacy shell defaulted to Double. Mixing shells can therefore change stored BSON types. (low confidence)
When a script establishes its own connection, --nodb prevents the shell from making its initial connection on startup. (high confidence)

Use mongosh --file script.js (or -f) for command-line scripts, and load("script.js") within an existing shell session. The CLI supports executing scripts without entering the interactive console. (high confidence)

Legacy-shell migration requires script review. Studio 3T identifies native JavaScript function changes, Percona warns that legacy methods can be unavailable or replaced, and MongoDB enumerates deprecated helpers. (high confidence)

Database-call results cannot be used in ordinary class constructors, non-async generators, Array.sort callbacks or class setters as if all JavaScript contexts supported shell database evaluation. The compatibility reference gives async or precomputation alternatives. (low confidence)

Studio 3T's October 2022 migration announcement states that Query Assist support introduced in 2022.9 required its bundled mongosh; non-bundled mongosh lacked Query Assist and inline editing in that integration. This is historical product-specific behavior, not a current universal mongosh limitation. (low confidence) (verified as of 2022-10-31)

In Microsoft's Azure migration troubleshooting procedure, successful TCP connectivity followed by mongosh TLS or authentication failure directs investigation to certificate settings or credentials/authentication database. The probe must run from the relevant network position; success from an arbitrary workstation does not establish migration-service reachability. (low confidence)

The official cheat sheet is explicitly incomplete; full coverage requires the Database Commands and mongosh Methods references. Import/export and dump/restore utilities run in the system terminal rather than as mongosh methods. (low confidence)

A historical July 2023 VS Code issue reports CommandNotFoundException for mongosh despite a working executable elsewhere. It establishes an integration launch symptom, without proving its cause or a current product defect. (low confidence)

To make administrative scripts portable, select the database with db.getSiblingDB("name") and supply host and port on the command line rather than embedding a deployment address in the script. (high confidence)
mongoimport, mongoexport, mongodump and mongorestore are separate Database Tools commands executed in the system terminal, rather than mongosh methods. (low confidence)

A connection URI or --host/--port selects the deployment; --username and --authenticationDatabase select authentication details, and omitting the password allows an interactive prompt. (high confidence)

For portable scripts, select the database with db.getSiblingDB() and supply deployment details on the command line. If the script creates its own connection, --nodb avoids an initial automatic connection. (low confidence)
mongosh reads .mongoshrc.js from the user's home directory on startup; --norc suppresses that startup file. A legacy .mongorc.js is not automatically loaded as a substitute. (high confidence)
Built-in .editor mode accepts multiline code: Ctrl-D runs the code and Ctrl-C cancels it; declarations remain in the shell’s global scope afterward. (low confidence)
MongoDB documents try/catch with exit(code) for scripts that must terminate after exceptions or unexpected results. (low confidence)

For connection checks, db.runCommand({ping: 1}) is a concrete shell probe; Microsoft demonstrates running it noninteractively with mongosh "$SOURCE_URI" --eval and expects { ok: 1 }. (high confidence)
load() accepts relative and absolute paths but has no search path: a relative script must exist under the shell's current working directory at the supplied path. (low confidence)

The compatibility reference deprecates count(), insert(), remove(), save() and update() in favor of explicit methods such as countDocuments()/estimatedDocumentCount(), insertOne()/insertMany(), deleteOne()/deleteMany(), and updateOne()/updateMany(). (low confidence)
